summary:
RETRO-V-ASTROCARE, developed by Team Retro-V, is an interactive digital health-monitoring platform designed to support astronaut health and well-being during space missions. Spaceflight exposes astronauts to unique health challenges, including microgravity-related physiological changes, radiation exposure, sleep disturbances, and psychological stress.

RETRO-V-ASTROCARE aims to make astronaut health information easier to understand through an interactive dashboard, visual health indicators, human anatomy visualization, and accessible space-health information. The platform brings together relevant scientific knowledge and health-related datasets to demonstrate how physiological changes and spaceflight hazards can be explored and monitored.

By transforming complex health information into an understandable and engaging digital experience, RETRO-V-ASTROCARE promotes awareness of the challenges of human spaceflight and highlights the importance of continuous health monitoring for future exploration missions. Our goal is to contribute to safer, healthier, and more sustainable human exploration of space.

RETRO-V-ASTROCARE – Supporting Human Health Beyond Earth

Developed by Team Retro-V | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

1. Introduction

Human space exploration introduces significant challenges to astronaut health. The absence of Earth's normal gravity, exposure to space radiation, changes in sleep patterns, isolation, and other environmental conditions can affect multiple physiological systems.

RETRO-V-ASTROCARE is an interactive digital health-monitoring and awareness platform developed to explore these challenges and communicate the importance of astronaut health management during space missions.

Our project focuses on making space-health information more accessible through a user-friendly digital experience that combines scientific information, health indicators, data visualization, and interactive anatomical representations.

2. Main Features and Functionality

2.1. Interactive Health Dashboard

ASTROCARE provides a centralized health monitoring dashboard where users can explore astronaut health indicators and understand how different physiological measurements contribute to astronaut well-being. It displays health summaries, subsystem conditions, important alerts, mission information, and real-time changes in health indicators.

2.2. Human Anatomy Visualization

The platform incorporates interactive 3D human-body visualization that allows users to explore different anatomical structures and physiological systems. Users can select specific body regions, inspect anatomical details, and understand how spaceflight conditions may affect different parts of the human body.

2.3. Health Data Visualization

Relevant health datasets and scientific information are used to demonstrate how health measurements can be organized, interpreted, and presented through visual elements such as graphs, indicators, charts, and statistical summaries.

2.4. Spaceflight Health Awareness

The platform presents information about major human-spaceflight health hazards, helping users understand the potential effects of microgravity, radiation, isolation, and other mission-related conditions on astronaut health.

2.5. User-Friendly Interface

ASTROCARE is designed with an accessible and interactive interface that organizes complex health information into understandable sections. Its responsive layout supports both desktop and mobile devices.

2.6. Multiple Mission Operation Modes

The system provides two main operating modes:

  • In-Flight Mode: Focuses on astronaut health monitoring, physiological measurements, subsystem assessments, and mission health alerts.
  • Recovery Mode: Focuses on post-mission rehabilitation, physical recovery, exercise activities, and monitoring astronaut readiness to return to Earth.

2.7. Physiological Subsystem Monitoring

Users can explore and monitor different physiological systems through dedicated health indicators and measurements, including:

  • Cardiovascular system
  • Ocular and neuro-visual system
  • Musculoskeletal system
  • Mood and sleep-related indicators

The platform evaluates these measurements to provide an overview of each subsystem's health condition.

2.8. Health Risk Assessment and Triage System

ASTROCARE incorporates a rule-based health assessment system that evaluates physiological measurements and identifies potential health risks. It categorizes health conditions into different severity levels, including normal, warning, and critical conditions, helping users recognize potential health concerns.

2.9. Interactive Health Metrics and Simulation

Users can modify physiological measurements through interactive controls and observe how changes affect health assessments. The platform also provides predefined simulation cases, including normal, warning, and critical scenarios, for demonstrating different health conditions.

2.10. Mission Environment Selection

The system allows users to select different mission environments and explore how environmental conditions influence astronaut health measurements and physiological risk assessments.

2.11. Daily Health Logging and Mission Records

Users can record daily astronaut health information, including exercise performance, sleep duration, and other mission-related measurements. The recorded information is maintained in a mission log archive for reviewing previous entries and monitoring changes over time.

2.12. Health Data Import and CSV Processing

ASTROCARE supports uploading health datasets in CSV format. The system processes uploaded files, validates their structure, identifies supported health measurements, and organizes the imported information for visualization and analysis.

Users can also review dataset information, processing results, and data validation errors.

2.13. Interactive Health Analytics

The platform provides a dedicated health analytics section that presents health measurements through interactive charts and statistical visualizations. Users can explore different health indicators, switch between available chart categories, and examine trends across different time periods.

2.14. Health Trend Analysis and Insights

The system analyzes available health measurements and identifies trends, baseline deviations, and potential changes in physiological conditions. It presents observations and alerts using a local rule-based assessment system to support the interpretation of astronaut health data.

2.15. NASA Space Weather Integration

ASTROCARE incorporates NASA Space Weather Database of Notifications, Knowledge, Information (DONKI) integration to retrieve relevant space-weather information, including Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) events.

The platform provides access to available space-weather event information and supports offline simulation when live data cannot be retrieved.

2.16. Post-Mission Rehabilitation Management

The Recovery Mode provides a dedicated rehabilitation workspace for monitoring astronaut recovery after returning from space missions. It includes recovery progress indicators, rehabilitation activities, physical condition assessments, and Earth-readiness tracking.

2.17. Rehabilitation Exercise Demonstrations

The system provides visual exercise demonstrations to help users understand how rehabilitation activities should be performed. It includes exercise illustrations, instructions, and activity-specific information.

2.18. Exercise Checklists and Progress Tracking

Users can follow rehabilitation exercise checklists, mark individual exercise steps as completed, reset activity progress, and track completed rehabilitation activities. Progress is saved so users can continue monitoring their rehabilitation activities.

2.19. Rehabilitation Session Management

ASTROCARE includes rehabilitation session management that allows users to complete structured exercise sessions and record their progress. Completing a rehabilitation session updates the recorded session count and contributes to the overall recovery readiness assessment.

2.20. Recovery Safety Assessment

The platform includes recovery safety monitoring through pain and dizziness assessments. These measurements are evaluated to identify potential safety concerns and determine whether rehabilitation activities should be paused.

2.21. Earth Readiness Assessment

The system calculates an astronaut's readiness to return to normal Earth conditions using mission records, rehabilitation progress, completed sessions, and recovery-related measurements. It provides a readiness overview to demonstrate the astronaut's recovery progress.

2.22. Mission Planning and Configuration

ASTROCARE provides a mission planning interface where users can review mission-related information, configure mission settings, select mission profiles, and explore the available operational parameters.

2.23. Space Weather Alerts and Notifications

The platform displays relevant space-weather information and important health alerts. Users can refresh available space-weather data and review the current data source status.

2.24. Interactive Data Source Information

The system provides information about uploaded datasets, processed records, chart associations, and available data sources. This helps users understand where displayed health information originates and how imported data is organized.

2.25. Customizable Dashboard Appearance

Users can select different dashboard background themes, including space-related visual environments, to customize the appearance of the platform.

2.26. Audio Notifications and Interface Feedback

ASTROCARE includes optional interface sound effects for user interactions, notifications, warnings, and important system events. Users can enable or mute the audio feedback.

2.27. Mission Information and Navigation

The platform includes organized navigation sections for accessing the main dashboard, mission information, operational workspaces, and team contact information. It also provides a mobile-friendly navigation interface for smaller screens.

2.28. Team Contact and Feedback

The website provides a contact section where users can submit messages and feedback to the development team. It also includes sections for team information and relevant contact channels.

2.29. Responsive and Interactive Design

The platform is designed to provide an interactive experience across different screen sizes. Its responsive interface adapts to desktop and mobile devices while maintaining access to the main dashboard, visualization tools, and operational features.

2.30. Local Data Storage and Progress Persistence

The system uses browser-based local storage to preserve selected information, including mission health logs, rehabilitation checklist progress, and dashboard theme preferences. This allows users to retain supported information when revisiting the website on the same browser.

2.31. Cloud Database Integration Using Firebase Firestore

ASTROCARE uses Firebase Cloud Firestore as its cloud-based NoSQL database to store, organize, and retrieve application data. It supports the management of astronaut health records, mission-related information, user data, and rehabilitation progress. Firestore enables data synchronization and persistent storage, allowing the application to access stored information across sessions.

Overall System Description

ASTROCARE is an interactive astronaut health monitoring and rehabilitation platform designed to demonstrate the monitoring, visualization, assessment, and management of astronaut health throughout space missions. It combines human anatomy visualization, physiological health monitoring, health data analytics, space-weather awareness, mission management, and post-mission rehabilitation into a centralized web-based platform.

3. NASA Data and Scientific Relevance

NASA's Human Research Program provides valuable scientific information about the risks associated with human spaceflight. ASTROCARE uses relevant NASA resources and datasets to connect its features with established space-health research.

The project aims to demonstrate how scientific datasets can be transformed into accessible visual information, helping users explore astronaut health challenges.

4. Benefits and Intended Impact

RETRO-V-ASTROCARE contributes to space-health awareness by:

  • Making complex astronaut health information easier to understand.
  • Demonstrating the importance of monitoring physiological indicators.
  • Connecting scientific datasets with interactive visualizations.
  • Improving public understanding of human-spaceflight health risks.
  • Encouraging interest in human health research and future space exploration.

The platform is an educational and demonstrative prototype, not a certified medical diagnostic or treatment system.

5. Technology and Development

RETRO-V-ASTROCARE was developed as a digital web-based application using modern development.

The development process involved interface design, interactive dashboard development, data integration, scientific research, and visual content creation.

The exact programming languages, libraries, frameworks, and services used are documented separately in our development resources.

6. Creativity and Innovation

The main creative aspect of RETRO-V-ASTROCARE is its effort to bring space-health research, anatomical visualization, and health-data presentation together in one interactive platform.

Instead of presenting scientific information only as lengthy documents, RETRO-V-ASTROCARE aims to make the information more engaging through visual exploration and an organized dashboard experience.

7. Conclusion

RETRO-V-ASTROCARE represents Team Retro-V's contribution to the future of human space exploration. By combining scientific resources, health information, and interactive digital technology, we aim to make astronaut health challenges easier to explore and understand.

RETRO-V-ASTROCARE – Because every journey beyond Earth begins with protecting human life.
